title: Supply & Demand Through the ICC Lens
hook: This isn’t stand-alone supply and demand. The higher-timeframe ICC tells the story first.

launchpad.outcome: Explain what each timeframe does in this strategy and name the full sequence: 3 Breaks, 2 Corrections, 1 Zone, 1 Retest.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Why does the zone only matter after the story and the sequence?

takeaways: Higher-timeframe ICC gives the direction. The 15M sets directional structure. The 5M builds the sequence, the zone and the entry.
The sequence is 3 Breaks, 2 Corrections, 1 Zone, 1 Retest.
Correction #2 creates the zone. BOS #3 activates it.
Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 or BOS #2 occurred.

slides.headline: This isn’t stand-alone supply and demand.
slides.line: Here, a zone only matters when the higher-timeframe story and a full confirmation sequence stand behind it.

slides.headline: Each timeframe has one job.
slides.line: Tap each one. Every timeframe answers a different question.

steps.label: 4H · Higher-timeframe context
steps.sub: What story is the bigger picture telling?

steps.label: 1H · ICC, structure and location
steps.sub: Where is price inside the structure, and what is the HTF ICC doing?

steps.label: 15M · Directional BOS or MSS
steps.sub: Has the 15M broken in the direction of the story?

steps.label: 5M · Corrections, continuation, the zone and execution
steps.sub: Does the sequence complete, and where is the zone?

slides.headline: 3 Breaks. 2 Corrections. 1 Zone. 1 Retest.
slides.line: Tap each card. This is the whole strategy in four lines.

cards.label: 3 Breaks
cards.sub: BOS #1 on the 15M, then BOS #2 and BOS #3 on the 5M.

cards.label: 2 Corrections
cards.sub: Correction #1 after BOS #1. Correction #2 after BOS #2.

cards.label: 1 Zone
cards.sub: Correction #2 creates it. BOS #3 activates it.

cards.label: 1 Retest
cards.sub: Price returns to the zone. That’s where the entry lives.

slides.kicker: Step 3 · The sequence on a chart
slides.headline: Watch the full sequence build, candle by candle.
slides.line: Bullish example. Press the button to print each part.

steps.caption: BOS #1. A 15M candle closes above the 15M level, in the direction of the higher-timeframe story.
Correction #1. On the 5M, price pulls back, preferably toward the original 15M break.
BOS #2. A 5M candle closes above the high Correction #1 pulled back from.
Correction #2 creates the zone: its last bearish candle. It’s only a potential zone for now.
BOS #3. A 5M close above the high Correction #2 pulled back from. Now the zone is active.
The retest. Price comes back to the zone. Only now does the entry model apply.

slides.headline: BOS #2 just printed. Is that your entry?
slides.line: Price is moving fast and it looks strong.

check.prompt: BOS #2 just closed. What do you do?

options.label: Enter now, the move is strong
options.feedback: Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 or BOS #2 occurred. Correction #2 hasn’t created the zone yet, and BOS #3 hasn’t activated it.

options.label: Wait for Correction #2, the zone, BOS #3 and the retest
options.why: Right. The zone comes from Correction #2, BOS #3 activates it, and the entry waits for the retest.

slides.quote: The zone isn’t the strategy. The sequence is.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what does each timeframe do, and what is the full sequence?
slides.modelAnswer: The 4H gives the higher-timeframe context, the 1H gives ICC, structure and location, the 15M gives the directional break, and the 5M builds the corrections, the zone and the entry. The sequence is BOS #1, Correction #1, BOS #2, Correction #2 (which creates the zone), BOS #3 (which activates it), then the retest.
